findings.title: Denial cache test does not actually verify precedence over perm cache
findings.body: In TestService_CacheCheck/"Should deny on explicit cache deny entry", the permCache is seeded with map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}. Because the value is false (i.e. the positive cache already encodes a deny), the assertion assert.False(t, resp.Allowed) would pass even if the new permDenialCache early-return in Check were removed: getCachedIdentityPermissions would return the cached scope map, checkPermission would return false on its own, the code would fall through to the DB (which has no userPermissions set in this subtest), and the response would still be Allowed=false. To actually exercise the precedence that the PR introduces (denial cache consulted before positive cache, denial wins), the seeded scope must be true (e.g. map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": true}); with that value, removing the permDenialCache branch would make the test fail. The inline comment "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked" is also misleading because the value being written is false, not true. As written, the test passes trivially and does not cover the new code path it is meant to cover.

findings.title: Negative cache for (user, action, name, folder) is never invalidated, producing a 30s stale-deny window after grants
findings.body: s.permDenialCache.Set is called whenever a DB-backed check returns Allowed=false for a concrete (namespace, userUID, action, name, parentFolder) tuple, but there is no corresponding Delete anywhere in the changed files (or the surrounding code referenced by the diff). The same cache is consulted at the very top of Check, before the positive permCache or DB is read. Consequence: if a user has previously been denied access to a specific (name, parentFolder) for a given action (e.g. they were not in a role/team that had access, or a prior transient store error returned an empty permission set), a later grant of permission on that exact resource (role assignment, team membership change, fix of a misconfigured permission, or any path that flips the DB row to allow) will not be reflected for up to shortCacheTTL = 30s — the Check call will short-circuit at line 117 and return Allowed=false even though the DB would now allow it. The PR's stated goal (letting freshly-created dashboards/folders be accessible) is fine because for newly created resources no prior denial can exist, but for any other grant path this introduces a 30-second window in which authorized users are spuriously denied. Either the denial cache must be invalidated on every permission/role/team mutation path, or the per-resource denial entry should not be persisted at all (the positive permCache miss already forces a DB lookup on the second branch added in this PR).

findings.title: requestCount metric labeled fromCache=true on the DB-resolved response path
findings.body: The final response path of Check (reached when getCachedIdentityPermissions returned a hit whose permission check failed and the request was re-resolved via getIdentityPermissions / DB) increments s.metrics.requestCount with WithLabelValues("false", "true", ...). The second positional label is fromCache throughout the rest of the file (e.g. the permDenialCache-hit branch at line 119 and the cached-allow branch at line 133 use the same "false","true" pair). On this last code path the answer was not served from cache, so labeling it fromCache="true" misrepresents the metric and will understate the DB/hit-miss ratio in dashboards/alerts. This label pair was already present before the PR, but the PR added a new "false" path (the post-permissionCache miss branch) that reuses the same labels, so the misleading attribution now also applies to requests that genuinely went through the new fall-through-to-DB logic.
